nodes.label: Phase 0a Follow-Ups Ledger
nodes.rationale: Everything found, judged and deliberately not done in Phase 0a, each item saying what it is, why it was left and what it costs to leave. Two execution passes on 2026-09-02 closed most of the self-contained subset; anything not marked Closed is still open.

nodes.label: Promoting lapidary-enterprise Out Of L3
nodes.rationale: The layering rule used to permit L3 to L3, so lapidary-api to lapidary-enterprise passed CI — an edge that would make the free application depend on the enterprise crate. Closed by giving enterprise its own tier: the edge is now rejected structurally with a violation message naming the product rule it protects, while enterprise to api stays legal.

nodes.label: FORBIDDEN_PAIRS Replaces A Comment
nodes.rationale: Removing the api-to-cad dependency left only a comment asserting the invariant, because edge_allowed(L3,L2) returned true unconditionally. A (from,to,why) triple list checked beside the tier rule now fails the edge structurally while leaving a different L3-to-L2 edge legal — a named pair, not a blanket ban. Proven to bite by adding the dependency back and watching the check fail. This is the mechanism for future prohibitions; edge_allowed operates on tiers and cannot express a single-pair exception.

nodes.label: SERVER_FEATURES As A Build Arg
nodes.rationale: Both services once built from the same Containerfile with --features mock-kernel hardcoded, so the binary serving the open path linked the kernel crate. The feature list became a build arg declared inside the build stage — a bare ARG before FROM would have been the wrong scope — set only by worker. Verified by reading each image's startup kernel line. Not the same as splitting the binary by role, which stays the real fix.

nodes.label: cargo xtask check-deploy
nodes.rationale: Checks that exactly the services in KERNEL_LINKED_SERVICES set SERVER_FEATURES, that the Containerfile's cargo build routes through the expansion rather than a hardcoded flag, and that ARG SERVER_FEATURES is visible to that build line across every stage. A fourth violation class catches the parser itself going stale, naming the function to fix rather than blaming the config. The check is static — it reads text, does not build an image, and its own failure message says so.

nodes.label: publish = false Enforced By check_publish
nodes.rationale: Setting publish = false on all 13 manifests let deny.toml use allow-wildcard-paths instead of a version pin on every internal path dependency, removing the coupling that required editing eleven lines on a version bump — but only a comment tied the two together, so a new crate would silently inherit the exemption. check_publish now fails any member whose cargo metadata publish field is not null, saying what to add and why.

nodes.label: Open: worker And api Are The Same Process
nodes.rationale: Correct for 0a's prove-the-topology goal, but Phase 1 needs a LAPIDARY_ROLE switch or a subcommand before the worker leases jobs, or the queue is served by two full HTTP routers and lapidary-server's 'api plus optionally in-process worker' description stays fiction. Splitting the images removed the kernel from the open-path artifact but did not give the worker its own identity.

nodes.label: Open: The Source-File Half Of The Open-Path Rule
nodes.rationale: The kernel half is closed twice over, but lapidary-api still depends on lapidary-storage, so nothing structural stops an open-path handler reading source bytes. A FORBIDDEN_PAIRS entry cannot express it: the crates must stay connected for derivatives, and the distinction is which bytes a handler reads, not whether the crates may be connected — a dependency-graph check only sees the latter. Needs an API-level boundary, such as a derivatives-only handle open-path handlers can hold and a source-reading one they cannot.

nodes.label: Open: KernelOutput Will Have To Change
nodes.rationale: Phase 0b needs blob references for the LOD ladder, and measurement cannot snap to opaque strings like 'CYLINDRICAL_SURFACE:22.000' — it needs axes, radii and normals. The change is cheap now, since mock.rs plus four tests are the only construction sites, and the mesh-yields-no-analytic-entities invariant survives any richer entity type. Only the sidecar README's false claim that the trait does not change was corrected; the redesign itself is open.

nodes.label: Open: Secrets Visible To docker inspect
nodes.rationale: Compose interpolates POSTGRES_PASSWORD into DATABASE_URL for api and worker, so the plaintext password is readable by anyone with engine access. Standard for compose without a secrets backend and not baked into an image layer; revisit with podman/docker secrets or an external manager when the fleet story lands.

nodes.label: Classifying Connect Failures By SQLSTATE
nodes.rationale: Every connect() failure used to map to Unreachable, so a wrong password read as 'could not reach the database'. Now classified into AuthenticationFailed, DatabaseMissing and Unreachable, each carrying only a redacted target, with a regression test asserting no rendered message leaks credentials.

nodes.label: Empty-State Copy Promised An Interaction That Did Not Exist
nodes.rationale: 'Drop a folder of STL or STEP files to begin' was untrue — nothing implemented dropping a folder. Reworded to something true today, with a regression test asserting the component renders the string so its use cannot drift silently. The ingest half stays open: Phase 1 shipping ingest and restoring a truthful call to action is an acceptance item.
